title: Keeping the shop window clear
target: How to keep the glass in a Supermarket Simulator shop presentable, given that windows, shards, dust and cleaning are all separate named pieces.
prerequisites: A shop with windows in it

steps.do: Know which pane is which before anything breaks.
steps.because: four shop windows are named, a front left and right beside a left and a right one (Window_Front_Left, Window_Front_Right, Window_Left, Window_Right)

steps.do: Replace a broken pane rather than covering it.
steps.because: each window has a shard version named beside it (Window_Front_Left_Shards, Window_Left_Shards)

steps.do: Clean the glass instead of replacing it when the problem is only dust.
steps.because: dust for glass is named with its own maps and a window is named as something that can be cleaned (M_Dust_For_Glass, Window Cleaning)

steps.do: Match a replacement to the glass the shop already uses.
steps.because: the glass is a material of its own with a colour sheet and a normal map (Glass_A, Glass_N, Glass_MS)

steps.do: Expect more than one grade of breakage.
steps.because: shards come with an easy, a medium and a strong version beside the plain set (Shards_Easy, Shards_Medium, Shards_Strong)

steps.do: Keep the display cases glassed as well.
steps.because: a showcase material carries a fade, a metallic smoothness and a normal sheet (Glass_Showcase, Glass_Showcase_Fade, Glass_Showcase_MS)

commonMistakes: Replacing a whole window when only the dust needed clearing.
Leaving a broken pane in place and losing the light it let in.
Ordering a pane without checking what the shop's glass is.
Forgetting that a display case is glassed too.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
